Vigilance

Vigilance is the unglamorous work of making sure that what the record says happened is what happened. That the hours were worked, the tonnes were carried, the concrete was tested and nobody was paid to look away.

NKovaya

What vigilance guards against

Bribery
Money or favours given or taken to win an order, pass an inspection, inflate a measurement, admit a vehicle or release a payment.
False records
Attendance for people who were not there. Hours for machines that did not run. Trips that were not made. Test results that were not obtained.
Theft and diversion
Material, fuel, scrap, tools or spares leaving a site that is not their own.
Cuts from wages
Anyone taking a share of a worker’s pay in exchange for the job or for anything else.
Collusion
Between our people and a client’s, a partner’s or a supplier’s, against the interest of any of them.
Concealment
Of an injury, a defect, a spill or a shortfall.
Extortion
Any demand for money under threat, by anyone.
Retaliation
Against someone who reported any of the above.

Who is responsible

Vigilance at ATKAYVA answers directly to the leadership of the firm. It is not delegated to a project, and no project manager can close a vigilance matter concerning their own job.

Every supervisor is responsible for the honesty of the records they sign. Every person who works under our name is expected to report what they see.

How wrongdoing is prevented

Most dishonesty in contracting happens at a small number of places: where something is counted, weighed, measured or approved. So that is where the controls are.

Attendance
Recorded each shift, signed by our supervisor, and wherever possible by the client’s representative too.
Machine hours
Logged on sheets signed at the end of each shift.
Weights
Taken on the weighbridge, with a slip for every load. Our totals are reconciled with the client’s each month.
Measurements
Taken jointly with the client’s engineer, as the work is done.
Tests
Carried out at accredited laboratories. Reports are original and traceable.
Payments
Made and received through the bank. Wages go to the worker’s own account wherever possible. We do not deal in cash beyond petty amounts.
Purchases
From approved sources, with more than one person involved in any order of size.
Partners
Verified before they join the network. See The standard.
Gifts
Declined, or declared. See Anti-bribery and gifts.

How it is detected

  • Reconciliation of our records against the client’s and the partner’s
  • Surprise checks at sites, weighbridges and stores
  • The weekly internal audits that already look at safety
  • Reports from workers, partners, clients and neighbours

The last of these finds more than the other three together. That is why the speak-up channel exists.

What happens to a report

  1. It reaches the leadership

    Directly. Reports are not filtered by the people they may concern.

  2. It is acknowledged

    Where the reporter has given a way to be reached, we aim to acknowledge within three working days.

  3. It is assessed

    Is there enough to look into? Is anyone in danger now? Does a client or an authority need to be told at once?

  4. It is looked into

    By someone with no stake in the matter. Records are secured. People are heard, including the person complained of.

  5. A decision is taken

    By the leadership, on the evidence.

  6. Action follows

    Correction of the record. Recovery of loss. Disciplinary action up to removal from the firm or from the network. A report to the client where their interest is affected, and to the authorities where the law has been broken.

  7. The reporter is told

    That the matter was dealt with, as far as fairness to others allows.

Working with a client’s vigilance

Many of our clients have vigilance departments of their own. Where a matter touches a client’s people or property, we inform the client and cooperate with their inquiry. We do not investigate a client’s employees ourselves.

If you work for a client and believe that someone from ATKAYVA has offered or given anything improper to a colleague, please tell your own vigilance department and tell us.

A week in October

Each year, in the week of 31 October, the birthday of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, India observes Vigilance Awareness Week. Sardar Patel was a son of Gujarat, and the country remembers him as the man who would not bend.

We mark the week by reading these rules aloud at every site, in the languages spoken there.

The pledge

I will do my work honestly. I will not give or take a bribe. I will not sign a record I know to be false. I will not stay silent when I see a wrong. I will protect the person who speaks.

Report a concern

To the leadership, in confidence. With your name or without it.

Speak-up and whistle-blower protection
Revision
0, October 2026
Owner
The Leadership
Applies to
Everyone

Purpose

To make sure that anyone who sees a wrong connected with ATKAYVA can report it to the leadership of the firm, safely and directly, and that the report is taken seriously.

Who may speak up

Anyone.

  • An employee or member of the core team
  • A worker on the register, or employed by one of our contractors
  • A machine owner, transporter, supplier or consultant
  • A client’s employee
  • A job applicant
  • A neighbour or member of the public

What to report

  • A demand for money or a bribe, by anyone, for anything
  • A cut taken from a worker’s wages
  • False bills, attendance, measurements, weights or test reports
  • Theft or misuse of material, fuel, tools or scrap
  • An unsafe act or an injury that is being hidden
  • Harassment, threats or abuse
  • A conflict of interest that has been concealed
  • Child labour or forced labour
  • Harm to the environment
  • Retaliation against someone who spoke up
  • Anything else that you believe breaks the law or our code

A complaint about your own wages, hours or working conditions can also be taken to the worker help desk, which is usually quicker.

How to report

Use the page at the foot of this page. It prepares a written report. Nothing is sent from this website by itself. You choose how to send it.

In writing
Fill in the page below. Send the report it prepares by WhatsApp, by email, or by post marked Confidential, for the Leadership.
By telephone
Call the number on the Contact page and ask to speak to the leadership about a confidential matter.
In person
Ask to meet a partner. You may bring someone you trust.

If you wish to stay unnamed

WhatsApp shows your number, and email shows your address. To stay unnamed, copy the report and send it by post, or from an account that does not identify you. This website does not record who you are, and it keeps nothing you type on this page once you leave it.

What to include

As much as you safely can.

  • What happened
  • Where and when
  • Who was involved, by name, role or description
  • How you know
  • Whether anything supports it: a slip, a message, a photograph, a witness
  • Whether you have told anyone else

Do not take risks to gather evidence. Do not confront the person. Tell us what you know and leave the inquiry to us.

Confidentiality

Your identity is known only to the leadership handling the report, and to anyone they must involve in order to look into it. It is not disclosed to the people you have named.

It may have to be disclosed if the law requires it, for example if the matter goes before a court. If that becomes likely we will tell you first.

Reports without a name

An unnamed report is read and acted on. It is harder to look into, because we cannot ask you questions, so please give as much detail as you can. If you can find a safe way for us to reach you, tell us what it is.

Protection

Nobody who reports a concern in good faith will be dismissed, demoted, denied work, removed from the register, struck from the network, threatened or otherwise punished for doing so. This holds even if the concern turns out to be mistaken.

Retaliation is itself a serious breach of our code. Anyone who retaliates, or who tries to find out who made a report, will face disciplinary action, whatever their position.

If you believe you are suffering retaliation, tell the leadership at once, by any of the routes above.

Good faith

Good faith means that you believe what you are reporting is true. You do not have to be right.

A report that the reporter knows to be false, made to harm someone, is not protected, and may itself lead to action.

What happens next

The steps are set out on the vigilance page. In short: your report reaches the leadership directly, is acknowledged if you can be reached, is looked into by someone with no stake in it, and is decided on the evidence. You are told that it was dealt with, as far as fairness to others allows.

If the concern is about the leadership of the firm

Say so in the report, and address it by name to another partner. A partner does not take part in looking into a report about themselves.

Other routes

This policy does not take away any right the law gives you. You remain free to go to the police, to the labour authorities, to a court, or to the vigilance department of the client in whose plant the matter arose. A crime should be reported to the police.

Records and review

Reports and their outcomes are kept in confidence by the leadership. This policy is reviewed once a year.

Write your concern

This form needs JavaScript. You can also reach us from the Contact page.

Fraud alert

Cheats use the names of real firms. If someone claiming to act for ATKAYVA has asked you for money, sent you a job offer you did not apply for, or told you our bank account has changed, read this page before you do anything else.

Three things ATKAYVA never does

We never charge a fee for a job, an interview, a medical, a uniform, a gate pass or a place on our register. We never ask for a deposit against a work order or a vendor registration. We never change our bank details by a message or an email alone.

Fake jobs

This is the commonest fraud of all, and it preys on people who can least afford it.

How it works
A message, a call or a letter offers work with ATKAYVA, often at a wage that is too good. Then comes a request for a “registration fee”, a “security deposit”, money for a “medical” or a “uniform”, or a payment to an “agent”.
The truth
We do not use recruiting agents. We do not charge anything, at any stage, to anyone. See How we hire.
What to do
Do not pay. Do not send your documents. Call the number on the Contact page and ask whether the offer is real.

Fake orders and enquiries

How it works
A supplier receives a purchase order or an urgent enquiry in our name, from an unfamiliar number or email address, asking for goods on credit to be delivered somewhere other than our site.
The truth
Our orders come from the email address and telephone number on this site, and deliveries are made to sites we can show you.
What to do
Before you despatch anything, call us.

Fake bank details

How it works
A client receives an email, apparently from us, saying that our bank account has changed and asking that the next payment go to a new one.
The truth
We notify bank details only on our letterhead, from the email address on this site, and we confirm them by telephone on the number on this site.
What to do
Do not change anything on the strength of a message. Call the number you already hold for us, not one given in the message.

Someone from ATKAYVA asking for money

How it works
A person who really does work with us, or says so, asks you for money: to pass your bill, to put your machine on a job, to give you work, to sign your attendance, to issue your gate pass.
The truth
That is a bribe or a cut. It is forbidden, whoever asks. See Anti-bribery and gifts.
What to do
Do not pay. Tell the leadership.

How to check that it is really us

There is one place where our telephone number, email address and postal address are published, and that is the Contact page of this site. A number or an address that reaches you any other way is not ours until you have checked it there.

The number, WhatsApp, the email address and the postal address are all on one page.

Contact

If a message, letter or caller uses any other number, address or email for ATKAYVA, treat it as false until we have confirmed it.

If you have already paid

  • Tell your bank at once, and ask whether the payment can be stopped or recalled.
  • Report it to the police, and to the national cyber-crime helpline on 1930.
  • Keep every message, number and receipt.
  • Tell us, so that we can warn others.

We cannot return money that was paid to a cheat using our name. We can help you with the facts the police will ask for.

Seen our name misused?

Every report helps us warn the next person.

Tell usContact details

Code of conduct
Revision
0, October 2026
Owner
The Leadership
Applies to
Everyone working under the ATKAYVA name

Work safely

Follow the life-saving rules and the rules of the plant you are in. Wear your protective equipment. Stop a job that looks unsafe. Report every injury and near miss.

Tell the truth

In what you say and in what you sign. Do not record an hour that was not worked, a trip that was not made or a test that was not done. If something has gone wrong, say so at once.

Give and take nothing improper

No bribes, in either direction. No cuts, commissions or favours. See Anti-bribery and gifts.

Keep your interests in the open

If you or your family stand to gain from a decision you are part of, say so and step back. See Conflicts of interest.

Treat people with respect

No abuse, no threats, no harassment, no insult to anyone’s caste, religion, region, language or sex. See Respect at work.

Deal fairly

With clients, partners, suppliers and each other. Measure honestly. Pay what is owed, when it is owed. Do not take advantage of anyone’s ignorance or need.

Guard what is not yours

A client’s plant, material, tools and information are the client’s. Take nothing from a site that you did not bring to it. Do not talk about a client’s plant outside it. Take no photographs inside a plant without permission.

Come fit for work

Sober, rested and well enough to be safe. No alcohol or drugs on site or before a shift.

Look after the place

Do not waste water, spill oil, burn rubbish or leave a mess. Drive carefully through villages. Leave wildlife alone. See Environment and Lion country.

Follow the law

The labour laws, the traffic laws, the tax laws and the plant’s rules. If a rule seems wrong, ask. Do not ignore it.

Use the firm’s name honestly

Do not use the name of ATKAYVA for private business. Do not make promises on its behalf that you have no authority to make. Do not speak to the press about a client or a site.

Speak up

If you see any of these rules broken, by anyone, tell your supervisor or tell the leadership. You will be protected. See Speak up.

If the code is broken

A breach is looked into fairly, and the person concerned is heard. Depending on what is found, the outcome may be advice, retraining, a warning, recovery of loss, removal from a site, removal from the firm or the network, or a report to the authorities.

Ignorance of the code is no defence. Nor is an instruction from a superior. A supervisor who orders a breach is more to blame than the person who carries it out.

One question to ask

When the code does not cover a case, ask yourself this. Would I be content for the leadership, the client and my own family to see exactly what I am about to do?

If the answer is no, do not do it.

Anti-bribery, gifts and hospitality
Revision
0, October 2026
Owner
The Leadership
Applies to
Everyone working under the ATKAYVA name

The rule

Nobody acting for ATKAYVA may offer, promise, give, ask for or accept anything of value in order to obtain or reward an improper advantage.

“Anything of value” means money, and it also means gifts, loans, discounts, travel, entertainment, a job for a relative, free work on someone’s house, or the use of a vehicle.

What this forbids

  • Paying a client’s employee to place an order, approve a bill, pass an inspection or overlook a defect
  • Paying a public official for a licence, a permit, a clearance or to avoid a penalty
  • Small payments to speed up a routine service
  • Taking money or favours from a machine owner, transporter, contractor or supplier in return for work
  • Taking a cut from a worker’s wages
  • Paying or receiving a kickback through a third party, a relative or an inflated bill
  • Asking a partner or supplier to pay a bribe on our behalf

Bribing a public servant is a crime under Indian law, and a firm can be held responsible for a bribe paid by someone acting for it.

Gifts and hospitality

India is a hospitable country, and work here runs on tea. We do not wish to forbid ordinary courtesy. We wish to prevent obligation.

AspectAcceptableNot acceptable
At a meetingTea, water, a working lunchA lavish meal, drinks, entertainment
At a festivalA box of sweets or a diary of modest value, given openly to the team and sharedCash in any amount. Gold or silver. Gift vouchers. Anything sent to a person’s home.
From a supplierA calendar, a penA phone, a holiday, a loan, a discount for personal purchases
To a client’s employeeNothing beyond the courtesy aboveAnything while an order, a measurement or a bill is pending
To a public officialNothingAnything

If in doubt, apply three tests. Is it small? Is it open? Would it embarrass anyone if it were known? If you are still in doubt, decline politely and tell your project manager.

A gift that cannot be declined without offence is accepted on behalf of the firm, reported to the leadership and shared or given away.

Envelopes at Diwali

It is a custom in parts of this trade for contractors to send something round at Diwali, and for something to be expected. We send our good wishes and, where it is the custom, a box of sweets to the office, addressed to everyone.

We do not send envelopes. Our partners and suppliers are asked not to send them to our people. Anyone who is pressed for one may refuse in the firm’s name, and will be supported.

Agents and intermediaries

We do not employ agents to win work. Nobody is authorised to act as a go-between for ATKAYVA with a client or an authority, and anyone who claims to be should be reported.

Donations and politics

The firm makes no political contributions. A charitable donation is never made at the request of someone who is in a position to give or withhold business, or as a condition of anything.

Records

Every payment the firm makes is recorded for what it is. There are no off-book accounts and no payments described as something else.

If you are asked for a bribe

  1. Refuse

    Politely and plainly. Say that the firm does not permit it.

  2. Do not argue or threaten

    Leave the conversation.

  3. Report it the same day

    To your project manager or to the leadership. If the demand came from a client’s employee, we will take it up with the client’s management.

  4. If work is being held up because you refused

    Tell the leadership. The firm will bear the delay. It will not pay.

A demand made with a threat to your safety is a different matter. Protect yourself first, then report it at once.

If the rule is broken

Giving or taking a bribe leads to removal from the firm or the network, recovery of what was lost, and a report to the client and the authorities.

Conflicts of interest

0, October 2026
Owner
The Leadership
Applies to
Partners, core team and anyone who decides or records on our behalf

What a conflict is

A conflict of interest arises when a person who is making or influencing a decision for ATKAYVA could gain or lose personally by it, or has a relative or close friend who could.

The danger is not that the person will certainly act wrongly. It is that nobody can be sure they did not.

Where conflicts arise with us

We are a network of local people, and we are open about what that means.

Choosing a partner
A supervisor recommends a machine, a truck or a labour contractor belonging to a relative.
Recording
A supervisor signs the attendance, hours or trips of a relative’s crew or machine.
Buying
A storekeeper or engineer orders from a supplier in whom they or their family have an interest.
Hiring
A place on the register or the core team is given to a relative ahead of someone better.
A second business
A member of the core team owns a machine or vehicle that works for us, or runs a business that supplies us.
A client’s employee
A partner or supplier of ours is related to someone at the client who decides on our work.
Gifts
See Anti-bribery and gifts.

The three duties

  1. Disclose

    Tell your project manager or a partner, in writing, as soon as you know that a conflict exists or may arise. It takes two lines.

  2. Step back

    Do not take part in the decision, the recommendation, the measurement or the signing. Someone else does it.

  3. Keep the record

    The disclosure and what was done about it are noted, so that the matter can be explained if anyone asks.

What is allowed

A relative may join the network, if the asset is inspected and the rate is set by someone who is not related. A relative may be hired, if someone else makes the choice on merit. A member of the core team may own a machine that works for us, if the leadership have agreed and someone else books and records it.

Most conflicts, once disclosed, are easily managed. An undisclosed conflict is treated as a breach of the code even if no harm resulted.

For the leadership

The leadership of the firm disclose their own interests to each other. No one in the leadership decides alone on a matter in which that person or a relative has a personal interest.

For clients

If you work for a client and are related to one of our people or partners, please tell your own management. We will tell them too, if we know.

A construction site is a rough place, and its language is not always gentle. There is a line all the same, and we hold it. Nobody who works under our name is to be abused, threatened, humiliated or harassed, by anyone, for any reason.

Respect at work, and prevention of sexual harassment
Revision
0, October 2026
Owner
The Leadership
Applies to
Everyone at our sites, offices, vehicles and accommodation

Dignity

Every person on our sites is owed the same respect: the engineer and the helper, the local and the migrant, the man and the woman, whatever their caste, religion, region or language.

We do not tolerate:

  • Abuse, shouting that turns to insult, or humiliation in front of others
  • Threats or violence
  • Insults or jokes aimed at a person’s caste, religion, community, region, language, sex, disability or appearance
  • Refusing work, water, food or a place to sit to anyone on such grounds
  • Withholding wages or documents as a means of control
  • Bullying of new workers, apprentices or young people

A supervisor may be firm. A supervisor may not be cruel.

Sexual harassment

Sexual harassment of women at the workplace is prohibited by Indian law, and by us.

It includes unwelcome physical contact or advances, a demand or request for sexual favours, sexually coloured remarks, showing pornography, and any other unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature, whether by action, words or gesture. It includes promising better treatment in return, threatening worse treatment for refusal, and making a woman’s work humiliating or unsafe.

The workplace includes the site, the office, the vehicle that brings her to work and the accommodation the employer provides.

How to complain

To whom
To our Internal Committee, where one is constituted for the establishment, or to the Local Committee of the district, as the law provides. A woman may also come directly to the leadership, who will help her reach the right committee.
When
The law asks that a complaint be made within three months of the incident. The committee may allow more time where there was good reason for the delay.
How
In writing. If a woman cannot write, the committee or a person she trusts will help her to.
What follows
The committee inquires, hearing both sides, and the law asks it to finish within ninety days. Its recommendations are acted upon by the employer.
While it is pending
She may ask for a transfer, for leave, or for the other person to be moved, and for her identity to be kept confidential.

Her identity, the identity of the person complained of and the proceedings are confidential by law.

Nobody may be punished for making a complaint or for giving evidence. A complaint that is not proved is not for that reason false.

Women on our sites

  • Separate, clean and lockable toilets
  • Transport that does not leave a woman as the last passenger on a night route, alone
  • No night work without her consent and proper arrangements for her safety
  • Equal pay for the same work
  • A supervisor she can speak to, and a route past that supervisor if need be

Everyone else

Men, too, can be harassed or bullied, and young workers of either sex are the most easily preyed upon. Any such conduct is a breach of our code and can be reported to a supervisor, to the worker help desk or through the speak-up channel.

What we do about it

A complaint is taken seriously, looked into quickly and fairly, and acted upon. The person complaining is protected from retaliation. A person found to have harassed or abused another is removed from the site and may be removed from the firm or the network, apart from any action under the law.

Labour standards
Revision
0, October 2026
Owner
The Leadership
Applies to
ATKAYVA and every labour contractor in its network

Age

Nobody under eighteen works on an ATKAYVA site, in any capacity. Age is checked against a document before a worker is admitted.

Freedom

All work is voluntary.

  • Nobody pays a fee or a deposit to get work with us or through us.
  • Nobody’s identity documents, certificates or bank passbook are held by the firm or by a contractor.
  • No advance or loan is used to tie a worker to a job.
  • A worker is free to leave, on reasonable notice, and is paid what is owed on leaving.

Wages

How much
Not less than the minimum wage fixed by law for the trade and the place. Skilled trades are paid for their skill.
When
On the day promised, and within the time the law allows.
How
Into the worker’s own bank account wherever possible.
With what record
A statement the worker can read: days worked, rate, overtime, deductions and the amount paid.
Deductions
Only those the law permits. Nothing for tools, protective equipment, gate passes or “commission”.
Equal pay
The same wage for the same work, for women and men.

Taking a cut from a worker’s wage, by anyone, is a matter for vigilance.

Hours and rest

  • Working hours, rest intervals and weekly rest as the law provides
  • Overtime is voluntary except in a real emergency, and is paid at the rate the law requires
  • No double shifts on work that can hurt someone
  • Rest days during a long shutdown are real

Statutory protection

Provident fund, state insurance and employees’ compensation cover as the law requires, with contributions deposited on time. Workers are helped to obtain and understand their account numbers.

Safety and health

Protective equipment is provided free. Induction and training are given in a language the worker understands. Medical examinations are arranged and paid for by the employer. See Safety.

Welfare

Drinking water
Clean and cool, at every work front.
Toilets
Clean, with separate ones for women.
Rest
A shaded place to sit and eat.
First aid
A stocked box and a trained person on every shift.
Accommodation
Where it is provided: weatherproof, ventilated and lit, with water, sanitation and a place to cook.

Workers from other states

Some skilled trades come from elsewhere in India. They are entitled to everything on this page, and also to help with the journey, a place to stay, and a way to be heard in a language they speak. Hindi is spoken by our supervisors.

Respect

See Respect at work.

A voice

A worker with a grievance may go to the supervisor, to the project manager, to the worker help desk or, in confidence, to the leadership through the speak-up channel. Nobody is penalised for raising one. Workers are free to associate as the law allows.

What we require of labour contractors

A contractor who supplies workers to us must hold the registrations and licences the law requires, keep the registers, pay as this page provides, and show us the proof. We check. A contractor who underpays, delays, deducts or conceals is removed from the network, and we make good to the workers what they were owed for work done on our jobs.

For the principal employer

The owner of a plant has duties in law towards the workers a contractor brings into it. We keep the records that allow those duties to be discharged, and we produce them when asked.

Partner and supplier code
Revision
0, October 2026
Owner
The Leadership
Applies to
Every partner in the network, while working for ATKAYVA

What we ask of you

Obey the law

Hold the registrations, licences, permits and insurance your business requires. Pay your taxes. Keep your papers current.

Work safely

Send only fit machines and trained people. Follow the life-saving rules and the rules of the plant. Your operator or driver may be stopped by our supervisor at any time, and must obey.

Treat your people properly

Meet the labour standards in full. Nobody under eighteen. Wages in full and on time. No fees, no cuts, no retained documents.

Be honest

Give true papers, true hours, true weights and true bills. Send the machine you promised, in the condition you described.

Offer nothing, and pay nothing

Do not offer money, gifts or favours to anyone at ATKAYVA or at a client. Do not pay if you are asked. Tell the leadership. See Anti-bribery and gifts.

Declare your connections

If you are related to someone at ATKAYVA or at a client who has a say in your work, tell us. See Conflicts of interest.

Carry legal loads

Do not overload. Cover and secure what you carry. Drive within the limit, and slowly through villages and after dark.

Respect the place

No dumping, no burning, no leaking machines. Leave wildlife alone.

Keep confidences

What you see inside a client’s plant, and what you learn of our rates and methods, stays with you. No photographs.

Do not sub-let without telling us

If the machine, vehicle or crew you send is not your own, say so before it arrives. It must meet the same standard.

Speak up

If you see something wrong on our job, by our people or anyone else’s, tell us. You will not lose work for it.

What you may ask of us

Payment as agreed
On the date promised, by bank transfer, against a clear statement. See Payments.
Fair counting
Hours, trips and weights recorded together and signed by both sides.
Clear instructions
What is wanted, where, when and for how long, before your machine moves.
A safe site
We will not ask your people to do what our own would refuse.
No demands
Nobody at ATKAYVA may ask you for money, a gift or a favour in return for work or payment. If anyone does, the leadership want to know.
A hearing
If you disagree with a deduction or a decision, a partner will hear you.
Loyalty
A partner who performs is called again.

If the code is broken

We will ask for an explanation and listen to it. Depending on what is found, we may ask for correction, withhold a disputed amount until it is settled, suspend you from the network or remove you from it. Where the law has been broken or a client harmed, we will report it.

Accepting the code

Every partner is given this code when joining the network, in Gujarati, Hindi or English, and accepts it by taking our work.
